answer: Uncertain. There may be a meteg under the alef (א), next to its qamats, but I can't confirm it from this image.
visible_evidence: The whole word ובואנו is in view, with the shuruk in the first vav and the holam on the second vav. Under the alef (the 4th letter from the right) there is a small cluster of marks: a short vertical stroke, a small mark to its left, and below them two small dots side by side. The cluster sits above the next line's ink and appears to belong to this word. At this resolution I can't tell whether the vertical stroke is the stem of the qamats or a separate meteg stroke. I also can't tell whether the two lower dots are part of a compound vowel, such as hataf-qamats, or something else. Nothing that looks like a meteg appears under the other letters (ו, ב, ו, נ, ו). Host letter: probably the alef if a meteg is present (low). Host vowel: qamats (low). Whether a meteg is present at all: undetermined (low).
